classical: The unexamined life is not worth living.
engineering: Code without tests is technical debt waiting to compound. Reflection through review keeps systems honest.
note: Socrates — on deliberate practice in engineering

classical: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
engineering: Consistent coding standards, automated pipelines, and daily refactoring compound into reliable systems.

classical: The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing.
engineering: The best engineers stay curious. Admitting gaps drives learning and prevents dangerous assumptions in architecture.

classical: No man ever steps in the same river twice.
engineering: Requirements change, teams evolve, technology shifts. Build systems that embrace change rather than resist it.
Ship incrementally, test thoroughly, roll back quickly. Production stability is a responsibility, not a constraint.

classical: Give me a lever long enough and I shall move the world.
engineering: The right abstraction at the right layer multiplies team velocity. Choose your levers wisely.
Understand your system's boundaries, failure modes, and performance characteristics before they surprise you in production.

classical: The beginning of wisdom is the definition of terms.
engineering: Clear type definitions, well-named interfaces, and shared domain language prevent entire categories of bugs.
note: Socrates — on TypeScript and domain modeling
